A.question: What is the story about?
A.explain_ko: 물고기 세 마리의 색과 빠르기, 먹이 주기 이야기. room·morning 은 지문에 한 번 나온 세부.

A.passage: I have a fish tank. It is in my room. I have three fish. One fish is red. One fish is yellow. One fish is blue and small. The red fish is fast. The blue fish is slow. I feed them every morning. I love my fish.
A.question: Which fish is slow?
A.explain_ko: The blue fish is slow. 빨간 물고기는 fast.

A.passage: It is Sunday. My family cleans the house. Dad washes the windows. Mom washes the car. My sister cleans the bathroom. I clean my desk. Our dog sleeps on the sofa. __He__ does not clean! Then we eat lunch together.
A.question: Who washes the car?
A.explain_ko: Mom washes the car. 아빠는 창문, 언니(누나)는 욕실을 청소한다.

A.passage: It is Sunday. My family cleans the house. Dad washes the windows. Mom washes the car. My sister cleans the bathroom. I clean my desk. Our dog sleeps on the sofa. __He__ does not clean! Then we eat lunch together.

A.question: 밑줄 친 부분의 소리가 다른 것은?
A.explain_ko: this 의 th 는 목소리를 내는 [ð], think·three·bath 의 th 는 바람 소리 [θ].

A.question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Ben and his dog _____ in the garden.
A.explain_ko: 주어가 Ben and his dog(둘)이므로 be동사는 are.

A.passage: My name is Jake. I am nine years old. I love my jump rope very much. I jump rope in the park every day. Today my friend Sam is with me. We are counting our jumps. Sam jumps forty times. I jump fifty times! Now we are drinking cold water under a big tree. Jump rope is fun and easy.
A.question: How many times does Jake jump?
A.explain_ko: I jump fifty times! forty 는 Sam, nine 은 Jake 의 나이.

A.passage: My name is Jake. I am nine years old. I love my jump rope very much. I jump rope in the park every day. Today my friend Sam is with me. We are counting our jumps. Sam jumps forty times. I jump fifty times! Now we are drinking cold water under a big tree. Jump rope is fun and easy.

choices: Jake's jump rope time with his friend
a big tree in the park

A.passage: Today is Saturday. It is snowing a lot. The trees are white. The roads are white, too. There are no cars on my street. My brother and I are making a snowman in the yard. We call him Snowy. He has a carrot nose and two stone eyes. Mom is taking pictures of us. My hands are cold, but I am very happy.
A.question: What is Mom doing?
A.explain_ko: Mom is taking pictures of us. 눈사람은 글쓴이와 남동생(형)이 만든다.

A.passage: Today is Saturday. It is snowing a lot. The trees are white. The roads are white, too. There are no cars on my street. My brother and I are making a snowman in the yard. We call him Snowy. A.question: Which is true about the story?
choices: There are no cars on the street.
A.explain_ko: There are no cars on my street. 오늘은 토요일, 코는 당근, 손은 차갑다.

A.question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
This watermelon is _____ than that one.
A.explain_ko: than 앞은 비교급. big 은 g 를 한 번 더 쓰고 -er → bigger.

A.question:
우리말에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
내 남동생은 학교에 노란 우산을 가지고 다닌다.
My little brother _____ a yellow umbrella to school.
A.explain_ko: 3인칭 단수 현재. 자음 + y 는 y 를 i 로 바꾸고 -es → carries. carried 는 과거.

A.question:
우리말에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
우리 개는 어젯밤에 저녁을 먹지 않았다.
Our dog _____ its dinner last night.
A.explain_ko: 과거 부정은 didn't + 동사원형. last night 이므로 doesn't·don't 는 시제가 틀린다.

A.passage:
Last Saturday, Lily spent a day with her aunt Rose. Aunt Rose is a zookeeper. It was a busy day. In the morning, they washed the elephant with a big brush. The elephant liked the cold water and moved its ears. After lunch, Lily gave fruit to the monkeys. The monkeys were noisy. One small monkey took a banana from her hand. Lily laughed. At the end of the day, she was very tired. But she smiled all the way home.

A.question: What is the story about?
choices: Lily's day at the zoo with her aunt
A.explain_ko: 사육사 이모와 동물원에서 보낸 하루. 코끼리 씻기·원숭이 바나나는 일부 장면.

A.passage:
Last month, many students asked for a cooking event. So we planned a Family Pancake Morning! It is on Saturday, May 10, at nine in the morning. It takes place in the school kitchen. Children make pancakes with their parents. We have strawberries, bananas, and honey for toppings. Each person pays three dollars. Children under seven do not pay. Please bring your own apron. Sign up at the school office by Wednesday. See you there!

A.question: What is this notice for?
A.explain_ko: 가족 팬케이크 아침 행사를 알리는 안내문. 학교 부엌·과일은 행사의 세부.

A.explain_ko: Please bring your own apron. 딸기·꿀은 학교가 준비한다.

A.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
나는 어제 쿠키를 구웠다.
A.explain_ko: yesterday 이므로 과거 baked(e 로 끝나면 -d 만). 목적어 cookies 는 동사 바로 뒤.

A.question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Look at those dark clouds. It _____ rain soon.
A.explain_ko: 주어 It + be going to + 동사원형. be동사가 빠지거나 are 이면 틀린다.

A.question:
우리말에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
아빠가 지금 부엌에서 감자를 자르고 계신다.
Dad _____ potatoes in the kitchen now.
A.explain_ko: 현재진행 is + -ing. cut 은 t 를 한 번 더 쓰고 -ing → cutting.

A.question:
우리말에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
나는 어제 공원에서 새 둥지를 발견했다.
I _____ a bird's nest in the park yesterday.
A.explain_ko: find 의 과거는 불규칙 found. finded 는 없는 말.

A.passage: Our class will visit Hill Park next Friday. We can go there by bus, by bike, or on foot. The bus is the fastest. It takes only ten minutes, but each student pays one dollar. A bike is slower than the bus. The ride takes about twenty minutes, and it is free. But some of our classmates do not have bikes. On foot, the trip is the longest of the three. It takes forty minutes, but it is free, too. And we will see the river and the old bridge on the way. In the end, our class chose the slowest way. It will be fun.
A.question: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 반은 다음 주 금요일에 Hill Park에 간다.
걸어서 가면 강과 오래된 다리를 볼 수 있다.
A.explain_ko: 1달러를 내는 것은 버스이고, 자전거는 무료(it is free)다.

A.passage: Our class will visit Hill Park next Friday. We can go there by bus, by bike, or on foot. The bus is the fastest. It takes only ten minutes, but each student pays one dollar. A.question: 이 반이 Hill Park에 갈 때 이용할 방법은?
A.explain_ko: 가장 느린 방법(the slowest way)을 골랐는데, 걸어가는 길이 40분으로 가장 오래 걸린다.

A.passage: My grandpa and I fly kites every spring. We make three kinds of kites together. The paper kite is the lightest of the three. It flies well on a calm day, but strong wind tears it. The plastic kite is heavier than the paper kite. It does not tear easily, and rain does not hurt it. The cloth kite is the most beautiful. Grandma paints flowers on it. But it is the heaviest, so it needs a strong wind. This Saturday, the wind will be very strong. So Grandpa says, "Let's take the _____ kite this time."
A.question: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 종이 연은 세 연 중 가장 무겁다.
플라스틱 연은 비에 잘 상하지 않는다.
A.explain_ko: rain does not hurt it(플라스틱 연). 종이 연은 가장 가볍고, 꽃은 할머니가 그리며, 토요일은 바람이 세다.

A.passage: My grandpa and I fly kites every spring. We make three kinds of kites together. The paper kite is the lightest of the three. It flies well on a calm day, but strong wind tears it. A.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
A.explain_ko: 토요일은 바람이 세고, 센 바람이 필요한 것은 가장 무거운 천 연. lightest 는 센 바람에 찢어지는 종이 연.

A.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
우리는 내일 동물원에 갈 것이다.
choices: We will going to the zoo tomorrow.
We will go to the zoo tomorrow.
We will goes to the zoo tomorrow.
We go will to the zoo tomorrow.
A.explain_ko: will 뒤에는 동사원형 go. going·goes 는 형태가 틀리고, will 은 동사 앞에 온다.

A.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
너는 수영장에서 뛰면 안 된다.
choices: You must not running at the pool.
You must don't run at the pool.
You must not run at the pool.
You not must run at the pool.
A.explain_ko: 금지는 must not + 동사원형. must 뒤에 don't 를 쓰거나 not 을 must 앞에 두지 않는다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 만나기로 한 시각을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Lucy, do you want to play badminton after school?
W: Sure. What time do you want to meet?
M: How about four o'clock at the park?
W: Sorry, I have a piano lesson until four.
M: Then let's meet at four thirty.
W: Hmm, it takes twenty minutes from my piano school.
M: Okay. Let's meet at five, then.
W: Great. I'll bring my rackets.
A.explain_ko: 4시는 피아노 수업, 4시 30분은 이동 시간 때문에 안 되어 5시로 정했다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 대화하는 장소로 가장 알맞은 곳을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Hello. May I take your order?
M: Yes. I'd like the tomato soup and a cheese sandwich.
W: Sorry, we don't have tomato soup today.
M: Oh, then I'll have the chicken soup.
W: Okay. Would you like some juice or tea?
M: Orange juice, please. Can I sit by the window?
W: Of course. Your food will be ready soon.
A.explain_ko: 주문을 받고(take your order) 수프·음료를 고르고 창가 자리에 앉는다 → 식당.

A.question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
A: Can I have some juice?
B: Sorry, there is _____ juice left. Let's buy some.
A.explain_ko: juice 는 셀 수 없는 명사이고 '거의 없다'는 뜻 → little. few·many·a few 는 셀 수 있는 명사에 쓴다.

A.question:
우리말에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
나는 아직 숙제를 끝내지 못했다.
I _____ my homework yet.
A.explain_ko: 현재완료 부정 have not + 과거분사. 주어 I 는 have, didn't 뒤는 동사원형.

A.passage: In autumn, squirrels get very busy. They collect nuts and hide them in the ground for winter. One squirrel can bury thousands of nuts in a single season. When snow covers the ground, it digs them up again and eats them. But squirrels do not _____ every nut. Some nuts stay in the ground because the squirrel forgets about them. In spring, these lost nuts start to grow into young trees. In this way, squirrels plant new trees without knowing it. So the next time you see a squirrel, remember that it is planting a forest.
A.question: 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 눈이 오면 다람쥐가 땅을 파는 방법
다람쥐가 잊어버린 견과가 새 나무로 자라나는 과정
A.explain_ko: 다람쥐가 잊어버린 견과가 봄에 나무로 자라 숲을 만든다는 글. 나머지는 앞부분 세부만 잡았다.

A.passage: In autumn, squirrels get very busy. They collect nuts and hide them in the ground for winter. One squirrel can bury thousands of nuts in a single season. When snow covers the ground, it digs them up again and eats them. But squirrels do not _____ every nut. Some nuts stay in the ground because the squirrel forgets about them. In spring, these lost nuts start to grow into young trees. In this way, squirrels plant new trees without knowing it. So the next time you see a squirrel, remember that it is planting a forest.
A.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
A.explain_ko: 겨울에 다시 파내지만, 잊어버린 견과는 땅에 남는다 → 모든 견과를 '찾지는' 못한다. hide·collect·bury 는 앞 문장 낱말.

A.passage: Every Wednesday, the sixth graders at our school visit the first graders. Each older student has a little buddy. They sit on the floor and read picture books together. At first, many sixth graders felt nervous because their buddies were very shy. But after a few weeks, the young children started to bring their favorite books. Now some of them even want to read aloud to their buddies. The teachers say that both groups enjoy this time a lot. The older students learn to be patient. The younger ones become braver at school.
A.question: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 6학년 학생은 각자 짝이 되는 1학년 학생이 있다.
선생님들은 두 학년 모두 이 시간을 즐긴다고 말한다.
A.explain_ko: 책을 가져오기 시작한 것은 몇 주가 지난 뒤(after a few weeks)다. 처음에는 수줍어했다.

A.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
우리 할아버지는 매일 아침 산책하는 것을 즐기신다.
choices: My grandfather enjoys to take a walk every morning.
My grandfather enjoys taking a walk every morning.
My grandfather enjoys take a walk every morning.
My grandfather enjoy taking a walk every morning.
A.explain_ko: enjoy 는 동명사를 목적어로 쓴다 → enjoys taking. 주어가 3인칭 단수라 enjoys.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 할 일로 가장 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Ben, have you finished your homework?
M: Yes, Mom. I finished it an hour ago. Why?
W: Your dad is cleaning the garage, and he needs some help.
M: Sure. Should I carry the heavy boxes?
W: No, Dad has already carried them out.
M: Then what can I do for him?
W: Please wash the two old bikes in the corner.
M: Okay. After that, I'll sweep the floor, too.
W: Thanks, but your sister will do that later.
M: All right. I'll go to the garage now.
A.explain_ko: 엄마가 낡은 자전거 두 대를 닦아 달라고 했다. 상자는 아빠가 이미 옮겼고, 바닥은 누나(여동생)가 쓴다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 축구 연습이 취소된 이유로 가장 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Hey, Kate. Why aren't you at soccer practice?
W: The coach canceled it this morning.
M: Really? Is it because of the rain?
W: No, the rain stopped an hour ago.
M: Then is the field too wet to play on?
W: No, it's fine. The problem is the air.
M: The air? What do you mean?
W: The weather report said the air pollution was very bad today.
M: Oh, I see. It's not good to run outside, then.
A.explain_ko: 비는 그쳤고 운동장도 괜찮다. 문제는 공기, 즉 대기 오염(air pollution)이 심한 것이다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 소방서 직업 체험 프로그램에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Jenny, did you see the notice about the fire station program?
W: No, I didn't. What kind of program is it?
M: Students can spend a day with real firefighters and learn what they do.
W: That sounds exciting. When is the program going to be?
M: It's on Saturday, November 8, from nine to three.
W: Do we need to bring anything special with us?
M: Just comfortable shoes and a water bottle. They'll give us lunch.
W: How many students can join it, by the way?
M: Only twenty, so we should sign up on the website by Friday.
A.explain_ko: 날짜(11월 8일), 준비물(편한 신발·물병), 인원(20명)은 나왔지만 참가비는 나오지 않았다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 대한 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Daniel, are these photos yours? They look amazing.
M: Thanks. I started taking pictures of birds last spring.
W: Really? How do you take such clear pictures of them?
M: I sit near the lake and wait quietly for a long time.
W: Don't you get bored when you wait that long?
M: Not at all. Watching birds is relaxing, and I can hear many sounds.
W: I'd like to try it, but I only have my phone camera.
M: That's fine. A phone is enough when you're starting.
W: Then could you show me where you usually go?
choices: No, I've never seen these birds before.
Yes, the camera was very expensive.
I took these photos with my phone.
Sure. Let's go to the lake together this Sunday.
A.explain_ko: 평소 가는 곳을 보여 달라는 부탁 → 이번 일요일에 같이 호수에 가자는 응답. 나머지는 사진·카메라 이야기로 엇나간다.

A.question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Good afternoon, students. This is Mr. Harris from the school cafeteria.
M: As you know, lunch lines have become very long, especially on Mondays and Fridays.
M: One main reason is that empty trays pile up near the exit, blocking the way.
M: So starting next Monday, we will try a new way of returning trays.
M: When you finish eating, please take your tray to the new carts by the windows.
M: Put the cups, spoons, and food waste in separate boxes on each cart.
M: Student volunteers will stand by the carts during the first week to help you.
M: With your cooperation, everyone will get lunch faster, so thank you in advance.
A.explain_ko: 다음 주 월요일부터 식판을 창가 카트에 반납하는 새 방법을 안내한다. 도우미 학생은 돕는다고만 했지 모집하지 않는다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람의 관계를 가장 잘 나타낸 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Excuse me. My bike makes a strange noise whenever I go up a hill.
M: Let me take a look. Hmm, the chain is quite loose, and it's covered in dust.
W: Can you fix it today? I ride it to work every morning.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

W: Right. And my coworker's son trained only in tennis from age seven and got hurt twice by twelve.
M: Still, I don't want him to give up every time something gets hard.

choices: 한 가지 운동에 집중해야 실력이 는다.
아이의 운동 종목은 부모가 정해 주어야 한다.
어린 나이에는 여러 운동을 경험해 보는 것이 좋다.
부상을 막으려면 준비 운동을 충분히 해야 한다.

A.question: Night Bug Walk에 관한 다음 내용을 듣고, 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.

B.explain_ko: 가슴 위에 올려놓는 것은 돌이고, 조개를 그 돌에 부딪쳐 깬다. 돌과 조개의 자리를 바꾼 문장이다.

B.passage: Before a long trip, many people put too many things in their suitcase. They are afraid of forgetting something important. However, a heavy bag can make your trip tiring. Here are a few tips for you. First, choose clothes in two or three colors, so you can wear them together easily. Second, roll your clothes instead of folding them. This saves space and keeps your clothes neat. Third, bring small bottles of shampoo, not big ones. Finally, leave some empty space in your bag. You may want to bring home some gifts from your trip.
B.question: 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 여행 선물은 출발 전에 미리 사 두는 것이 좋다.
여행 가방은 꼭 필요한 것만 담아 가볍게 싸는 것이 좋다.
옷은 여러 가지 색으로 다양하게 챙기는 것이 좋다.
여행에는 큰 샴푸 병을 가져가는 것이 경제적이다.
B.explain_ko: 무거운 가방은 여행을 지치게 하니 가볍게 싸는 요령을 알려 준다. 선물·옷 색·샴푸는 세부를 비틀거나 반대로 바꾼 오답이다.

B.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
내 꿈은 세계를 여행하는 것이다.
choices: My dream is travel around the world.
My dream is to traveling around the world.
My dream to is travel around the world.
My dream is to travel around the world.
B.explain_ko: '~하는 것' 보어 → to + 동사원형 to travel.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 대화하는 장소로 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Excuse me. Can my son touch the animals in this pool?
M: Yes, he can. But please use only two fingers.
W: What kind of animals are these? They look like stones.
M: They're sea cucumbers. And those pink ones are sea stars.
W: Wow, I've never seen a real sea star before.
M: Please don't lift them out of the water.
W: Okay. And where can we watch the penguins?
M: Go upstairs. Feeding time is at three.
B.explain_ko: 만지는 수조의 해삼·불가사리, 위층 펭귄 먹이 주기 시간으로 수족관임을 알 수 있다. 수영장은 pool, 해산물 시장은 sea cucumbers 에서 떠올리게 한 오답이다.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 동네 청소에 참여할 수 없는 이유로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Ben, are you joining the neighborhood cleanup this Sunday?
M: I really wanted to, but I can't this time.
W: Oh, do you have a soccer game again?
M: No, the season is over. My grandma is moving this weekend.
W: Really? Is she moving near your house?
M: Yes, just two blocks away. I'm going to help carry boxes.
W: That's nice. We'll miss you at the cleanup, though.
M: Please tell me about the next one.
B.explain_ko: 할머니가 이번 주말 이사하셔서 상자 나르는 것을 돕는다. 축구 시즌은 끝났고, 이사하는 사람은 남자가 아니라 할머니다.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
B.script:
M: Hello. I'd like tickets for the ferry to Gull Island.
W: Sure. A round trip is twenty dollars for adults and ten dollars for children.
M: Two adults and one child, please. My daughter is eight.
W: Kids under seven ride free, but she's eight, so she pays.
M: I see. And I have this coupon from our hotel.
W: Let me see. It gives you five dollars off the total.
M: Great. Can we also rent bikes on the island?
W: You can, but you pay for them on the island.
M: Okay. Then just the ferry tickets, please. Here's my card.
B.explain_ko: 어른 2명 40달러 + 어린이 1명 10달러 = 50달러, 쿠폰 5달러 할인 → 45달러. 50달러는 쿠폰을 빼먹은 값, 40달러는 딸을 무료로 본 값이다. 자전거는 섬에서 따로 낸다.

B.question: 다음을 듣고, Summer Reading Challenge 에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Hello, students. This is Ms. Carter from the Maple Street Library.
W: Our Summer Reading Challenge starts on July first and ends on August tenth.
W: Any student from grade one to grade nine can join for free.
W: Read ten books during the summer and write a short note about each one.
W: You can take home five books at a time with your library card.
W: Everyone who finishes the challenge will get a free ticket to the water park.
W: Please sign up at the front desk or on our website.
B.explain_ko: 기간(7월 1일~8월 10일), 대상(1~9학년), 상품(워터파크 입장권)은 나오지만 도서관이 몇 시에 여는지는 말하지 않았다.

B.question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
M: Good evening, residents of Willow Creek. This is Tom Baker from the town gardening club.
M: As you know, many of you grow vegetables and flowers in your yards every spring.
M: This year, our club is opening a seed library in the community center lobby.
M: It works just like a book library, but instead of books, you take home seeds.
M: You can take up to three packets of seeds each month without paying anything.
M: In the fall, we hope you will bring back some seeds from the plants you grew.
M: That way, the library will stay full for next year's gardeners.
M: The seed library opens on March fifth, so please stop by and pick your seeds.
choices: 주민 센터 로비 공사 일정을 안내하려고
B.explain_ko: 주민 센터 로비에 씨앗을 빌려 가는 seed library 를 연다고 알리는 방송이다. 동아리·주민 센터·가을은 방송에 나온 낱말로 만든 오답이다.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람의 관계를 가장 잘 나타낸 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Hello. My son's teddy bear lost an eye, and its arm is coming off.
M: Let me take a look. Oh, this bear has been loved for a long time.
W: It was mine when I was a child. Now my son sleeps with it every night.
M: I can sew the arm back on and find a matching button for the eye.
W: That would be wonderful. How long will the repair take?
M: Usually about a week, but I have many old toys to fix right now.
W: Could you finish it by Friday? My son keeps asking about his bear.
M: I'll try my best. I'll call you when your bear is ready to go home.
B.explain_ko: 남자가 곰 인형의 팔을 꿰매고 눈을 달아 주며 수리 기간을 말한다. 의사는 '아픈 인형'을 고치는 말투에서, 재봉 강사는 sew 에서 나온 오답이다.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
M: Amy, I noticed that you skipped your usual walk after lunch again today.
W: I had too many emails to answer, so I just ate at my desk.
M: I understand, but I think a short walk actually helps you work better.
W: Really? I thought staying at my desk would help me finish my work faster.
M: When you move for even ten minutes, more blood goes to your brain, and you think more clearly.
W: So that's probably why I always feel sleepy around three o'clock every afternoon.
M: Exactly. In my opinion, a quick break is not a waste of time at all.
W: Maybe you're right. Tomorrow, I'll put a walking break on my calendar.
M: Good idea. I'll join you, and we can walk around the park together.
choices: 점심은 책상에서 간단히 먹는 것이 좋다.
이메일은 오후에 한꺼번에 답하는 것이 좋다.
오후에 졸리면 잠깐 낮잠을 자는 것이 좋다.
점심 뒤 짧게 걷는 휴식이 일의 효율을 높인다.
B.explain_ko: 남자는 짧게 걸으면 뇌로 피가 더 가서 일을 더 잘한다고 한다. 책상에서 먹기·이메일은 여자의 상황, 낮잠은 언급되지 않았다.

B.question: 다음을 듣고, Young Inventors Fair 에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
M: Hello, everyone. I'm Kevin Ross, head of the science club at Oakwood High School.
M: I'm happy to announce our tenth Young Inventors Fair, which will be held on November twelfth.
M: Students in any grade can enter alone or in teams of up to three people.
M: Your invention must solve a real problem that you see at home or at school.
M: Each team will have a table to show its invention and explain how it works.
M: Judges from local companies will choose three winners, and each winning team will receive a 3D printer.
M: Please note that inventions using fire or sharp tools are not allowed for safety reasons.
M: To enter, send a short description of your idea to the science club by October twentieth.
choices: 최대 세 명까지 팀을 이룰 수 있다.
B.explain_ko: 우승 팀은 지역 회사에서 온 심사위원(judges from local companies)이 고른다. 나머지는 방송 내용과 같다.

B.question: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Hello, listeners. This is Laura Finch with Travel Notes, your weekly guide to smarter trips.
W: Many travelers try to visit as many cities as possible during a short vacation.
W: They spend hours on trains and buses, and they return home more tired than when they left.
W: Today, I'd like to suggest a different approach: staying in one place for a longer time.
W: When you stay in a single town for a week, you start to notice things that quick visitors miss.
W: You learn which bakery opens first, and the shop owners begin to greet you by name.
W: These small moments often become the memories you treasure most after the trip.
W: Of course, seeing famous sights is exciting, but rushing from one to another rarely lets you enjoy them.
W: So on your next vacation, choose fewer places and give yourself time to really live there.
choices: 여행할 때 한곳에 오래 머물면 더 깊은 경험을 할 수 있다.
짧은 휴가에는 기차보다 버스로 이동하는 것이 낫다.
유명한 관광지는 사람이 적은 이른 아침에 가야 한다.
여행 전에 현지 가게 정보를 미리 알아 두어야 한다.
B.explain_ko: 여러 도시를 서둘러 도는 대신 한곳에 오래 머물라고 권한다. 기차·버스, 유명 관광지, 빵집은 말 속 세부를 엮은 오답이다.

B.question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Hannah 가 Leo 에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
M: Hannah is volunteering at a beach cleanup on a sunny Saturday morning.
M: Her job is to walk along the shore with a group of children and pick up trash.
M: While they are working, a boy named Leo finds a pretty shell near the rocks and shows it to her.
M: He says he wants to take it home and put it on the shelf in his room.
M: Leo looks excited, and he is already holding the shell tightly in his hand.
M: Hannah looks closely at the shell and notices that a small hermit crab is living inside it.
M: The crab has pulled its legs inside, and it looks a little scared.
M: She knows that the crab uses the shell as its home and needs it to protect its soft body.
M: She also wants Leo to enjoy the beach without hurting any living things.
M: In this situation, what would Hannah most likely say to Leo on the beach?
choices: Leo, please put it back. Someone is living in that shell.
Leo, let's look for a bigger shell for your room.
Great job! Put it in the trash bag, please.
Be careful. The rocks are slippery near the water.
B.explain_ko: 껍데기 안에 소라게가 살고 있어 제자리에 돌려놓으라고 해야 한다. 더 큰 껍데기 찾기·쓰레기봉투·바위 조심은 상황 속 다른 낱말로 만든 오답이다.

A.hint_ko: [내가 집에 왔을 때, 고양이는 소파에 누워 있었다.] (과거진행형)
A.explain_ko: 과거진행 was + -ing. lie 는 ie 를 y 로 바꿔 lying

A.question: [write] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: This letter {} {} by my grandmother fifty years ago.
A.hint_ko: [이 편지는 50년 전에 우리 할머니가 쓰셨다.] (과거 시제)
A.explain_ko: 편지가 쓰인 것이므로 수동태 be + 과거분사. 과거라서 was written

A.question: [leave] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: When we arrived at the station, the train {} already {}.
A.hint_ko: [우리가 역에 도착했을 때, 기차는 이미 떠나 버렸었다.]
A.explain_ko: 도착한 과거보다 더 먼저 일어난 일 → 과거완료 had + left

A.question: [danger] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: The heavy snow made the mountain road {}.
A.explain_ko: make + 목적어 + 형용사(목적격 보어). 명사 danger → 형용사 dangerous

A.question: [who] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: I have a friend {} father is a firefighter.
A.explain_ko: friend 의 아버지 → 소유격 관계대명사 whose

A.question: [know] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: If I {} {} your phone number, I would have called you.
A.hint_ko: [내가 네 전화번호를 알았더라면, 너에게 전화했을 텐데.]
A.explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대 → If + had + 과거분사, would have + 과거분사

A.question: [do] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: Rarely {} my father come home before nine.
A.hint_ko: [우리 아버지는 9시 전에 집에 오시는 일이 거의 없다.] (현재 시제)
A.explain_ko: 부정어 Rarely 가 앞에 오면 도치 → 조동사 does + 주어 + 동사원형

A.question: 이것은 50년 전에 지어진 다리이다. (bridge, build, years, ago)
A.explain_ko: This is a bridge built 50 years ago. 과거분사 built 가 뒤에서 bridge 를 꾸민다

A.question: 위에서 보면, 그 섬은 하트처럼 보인다. (see, above, island, look, heart)
A.explain_ko: Seen from above, the island looks like a heart. 섬이 '보이는' 것이므로 수동 분사구문 (Being) Seen

A.question: 그 상자가 너무 무거워서 들 수 없으면, 우리는 아빠께 도움을 청할 것이다. (box, heavy, lift, ask, Dad, help)
A.explain_ko: If the box is too heavy to lift, we'll ask Dad for help. 조건절은 현재 시제, too + 형용사 + to부정사 = 너무 ~해서 …할 수 없다

B.question: [catch] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: My uncle {} a huge fish at the lake last Sunday.
B.hint_ko: [우리 삼촌은 지난 일요일에 호수에서 커다란 물고기를 잡으셨다.]
B.explain_ko: last Sunday → 과거. catch 의 과거형은 불규칙 caught

B.question: [swim] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: At 3 p.m. yesterday, the children {} {} in the river.
B.hint_ko: [어제 오후 세 시에, 아이들은 강에서 수영하고 있었다.] (과거진행형)
B.explain_ko: 과거진행 were + -ing. swim 은 단모음 + 단자음이라 m 을 한 번 더 써서 swimming

B.question: [hold] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: The school festival {} {} in the gym last Saturday.
B.hint_ko: [학교 축제는 지난 토요일에 체육관에서 열렸다.] (과거 시제)
B.explain_ko: 축제가 '열린' 것이므로 수동태 be + 과거분사. 과거라서 was held (hold-held-held)

B.question: [lose] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: Oh no! I {} {} my wallet, so I can't pay for this now.
B.hint_ko: [이런! 지갑을 잃어버려서 지금 이걸 계산할 수가 없어.] (현재완료)
B.explain_ko: 잃어버린 결과가 지금까지 이어짐 → 현재완료 have + 과거분사 lost

B.question: [health] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: Walking every day keeps your heart {}.
B.explain_ko: keep + 목적어 + 형용사(목적격 보어). 명사 health → 형용사 healthy

B.question: [who] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: The boy with {} I shared my umbrella is in my class.
B.hint_ko: [내가 우산을 같이 쓴 그 남자아이는 우리 반이다.]
B.explain_ko: shared my umbrella with the boy → 전치사 with 뒤의 목적격 관계대명사는 whom (전치사 바로 뒤에는 who·that 을 쓰지 않는다)

B.question: [bring] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: If you {} {} a map, we would not have gotten lost.
B.hint_ko: [네가 지도를 가져왔더라면, 우리는 길을 잃지 않았을 텐데.]
B.explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대 → If + had + 과거분사(brought), would have + 과거분사

B.question: [do] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: Little {} Minsu know that his friends were planning a party for him.
B.hint_ko: [민수는 친구들이 자기를 위해 파티를 준비하고 있다는 것을 전혀 몰랐다.] (과거 시제)
B.explain_ko: 부정어 Little 이 앞에 오면 도치 → 조동사 did + 주어 + 동사원형 know

B.question: 빨간 모자를 쓰고 있는 남자가 우리 코치님이다. (man, wear, red, cap, coach)
B.explain_ko: The man wearing a red cap is our coach. 현재분사 wearing 이 이끄는 말이 뒤에서 man 을 꾸민다

B.question: 열쇠가 없어서, 나는 집 밖에서 기다렸다. (not, have, key, wait, outside, house)
B.explain_ko: Not having a key, I waited outside the house. 이유를 나타내는 분사구문, 부정어 not 은 분사 앞에 둔다

B.question: 수영할 수 있을 만큼 날씨가 따뜻하면, 우리는 해변에 갈 것이다. (it, warm, enough, to, swim, go, beach)
B.explain_ko: If it is warm enough to swim, we'll go to the beach. 조건절은 미래라도 현재 시제, 형용사 + enough + to부정사 = …할 만큼 충분히 ~한

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Dad, the new aquarium opens this Saturday. Can we go?
M: Sure. I heard it has a huge shark tank.
W: Yes! And there's a sea lion show at two.
M: Great. I'll buy the tickets online tonight. It's cheaper.
W: Okay. Should I make sandwiches for lunch?
M: No, there's a café. Can you check the bus times?
W: Sure. I'll do it right now.
A.explain_ko: 아빠가 표는 자신이 사겠다며 여자에게 버스 시간을 확인해 달라고 했다. 표 사기는 아빠가 할 일, 샌드위치는 하지 않기로 했다.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __repair__
A.explain_ko: repair는 '수리하다'. 준비하다(prepare)·반복하다(repeat)·비교하다(compare)는 철자가 닮은 낱말의 뜻.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __refuse__
A.explain_ko: refuse는 '거절하다'. 재사용하다(reuse)·환불하다(refund)·제거하다(remove)는 re-로 시작하는 닮은 낱말의 뜻.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __무거운__
A.explain_ko: 무거운은 heavy. healthy(건강한)·hungry(배고픈)·happy(행복한)는 h로 시작해 -y로 끝나는 닮은 형용사.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
A.passage: There are _____ eggs in the fridge, so we need to buy more.
A.explain_ko: 셀 수 있는 복수 명사 eggs 앞에서 '거의 없는'은 few. little·much·a little은 셀 수 없는 명사에 쓰고, every 뒤에는 단수 명사가 온다.

A.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: He wants to become a doctor in the future.
My sister enjoys to swim in the lake every summer.
Learning a new language takes a lot of time.
If you are hungry, you can eat my sandwich.
She was late for school because she missed the bus.
A.explain_ko: enjoy는 동명사를 목적어로 쓰므로 enjoys swimming이 맞다. 나머지는 to부정사 목적어·동명사 주어·접속사 if·because가 바르다.

A.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage: After a hot shower, the bathroom mirror often turns white. You cannot see your face in it. Why does this happen? Hot water makes a lot of steam. Steam is water in the air, and it is warm. The mirror is cooler than the air in the room. When the warm steam touches the cool mirror, it changes into very small drops of water. These tiny drops cover the glass and make it cloudy. You can see the same thing on a glass of cold juice on a summer day. To keep your mirror clear, open a window before your shower.
choices: how to save water in the bathroom
why cold juice tastes better in summer
the best way to clean a glass mirror
why a bathroom mirror gets cloudy
the dangers of taking very hot showers
A.explain_ko: 따뜻한 수증기가 차가운 거울에 닿아 작은 물방울이 되어 거울이 뿌옇게 된다는 글. 주스·창문은 글에 나온 낱말을 쓴 다른 초점의 오답.

A.question: hourglass에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
A.passage:
An hourglass is an old tool for measuring time. It has two glass bulbs with a narrow neck between them. Sand runs slowly from the top bulb into the bottom one. When all the sand is at the bottom, a set amount of time is over. Long ago, sailors used hourglasses on their ships. Clocks with moving parts did not work well on rough seas. But sand always fell at the same speed. Sailors turned the glass every thirty minutes and rang a bell each time. People also used hourglasses in churches and kitchens. Today, you can still find small ones in board games.
* bulb: 둥근 부분
choices: 두 유리 부분 사이가 좁게 이어져 있다.
거친 바다에서는 움직이는 부품이 있는 시계가 잘 작동하지 않았다.
오늘날 보드게임에서 작은 모래시계를 볼 수 있다.
A.explain_ko: 선원들은 30분마다 모래시계를 뒤집고 종을 쳤다고 했으므로 '한 시간마다'는 틀리다. 이름 hourglass에서 나온 함정.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage: In Spain, many families eat dinner at nine or ten o'clock at night. Visitors from other countries are often surprised by this. But there are good reasons for it. Lunch is the biggest meal of the day. It usually starts around two. In summer, the afternoons are very hot. So many people take a long rest after lunch. Then they go back to work and finish at seven or eight. After such a big lunch, nobody feels hungry early in the evening. So the evening meal comes _____, and it is usually light. For many families, it is a quiet time to relax and talk.
A.explain_ko: 점심을 늦게 많이 먹고 일도 저녁 늦게 끝나므로 저녁 식사는 '늦게' 온다. early는 지문 낱말을 그대로 쓴 오답, first는 가장 큰 끼니가 점심이라는 말과 어긋난다.

A.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
나는 무척 피곤했기 때문에 일찍 잠자리에 들었다.
choices: I went to bed early because of I was very tired.
I went to bed early because I was very tired.
I went to bed early so I was very tired.
Because I went to bed early, I was very tired.
I went to bed early because I am very tired.
A.explain_ko: 이유를 나타내는 절은 접속사 because + 주어 + 동사. because of 뒤에는 명사가 오고, so·Because 위치를 바꾼 문장은 원인과 결과가 뒤바뀐다. 시제도 과거 was.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 오늘 지하철을 타는 이유로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Hi, Jenny. Don't you usually take the number 5 bus?
W: Yes, but the bus stop near my house is closed this week.
M: Oh, is it because of the road work on Maple Street?
W: No, that finished yesterday. They're painting a bike lane at the stop.
M: I see. So you have to take the subway for a while.
W: Right. It's ten minutes slower, but I can read on the train.
choices: 메이플 거리 도로 공사가 끝나지 않아서
집 근처 버스 정류장이 이번 주에 닫혀서
A.explain_ko: 자전거 도로를 칠하느라 집 근처 버스 정류장이 이번 주에 닫혔다. 도로 공사는 어제 끝났고, 지하철은 10분 더 걸린다고 했다.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __decrease__
A.explain_ko: decrease는 '줄어들다, 감소하다'. 증가하다(increase)·결정하다(decide)·묘사하다(describe)는 닮은 철자의 낱말 뜻.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __improve__
A.explain_ko: improve는 '향상시키다'. 증명하다(prove)·승인하다(approve)는 -prove가 들어간 낱말, 이동하다는 move의 뜻.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __설명하다__
A.explain_ko: 설명하다는 explain. explore(탐험하다)·expect(기대하다)·expand(확장하다)는 ex-로 시작하는 닮은 동사.

A.question: 다음 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
A.passage:
The city museum (A) _____ by a young architect in 1998.
I have a friend (B) _____ can speak four languages.
A.explain_ko: (A) 박물관은 설계'된' 것이므로 수동태 was designed. (B) 사람 선행사 a friend를 받고 뒤에 동사 can speak가 오므로 주격 관계대명사 who.

A.question: 어법상 __알맞은__ 문장의 개수는?
A.passage:
a. I have known Mr. Brown since I was ten.
b. The fresh bread smells wonderfully this morning.
c. Do you have anything cold to drink?
d. She went to the library to return the books.
e. We have watched that movie last Sunday.
A.explain_ko: a·c·d가 맞다. b는 감각동사 smell 뒤에 형용사 wonderful, e는 last Sunday와 현재완료를 함께 쓸 수 없어 watched가 되어야 한다.

A.question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage:
Why are tennis balls covered with fuzz? The fuzzy cover is made of wool or nylon. It has an important job. A smooth ball would fly through the air too fast, and players would find it hard to control. The fuzz catches the air and slows the ball down a little. It also helps the ball grip the strings of the racket for a moment. Because of this, players can add spin and decide where the ball will land. As a game goes on, the fuzz slowly wears away and the ball becomes faster. That is why balls are changed several times during a professional match.
* fuzz: 보풀
choices: Wool and Nylon: Materials for Every Sport
Why Professional Players Win More Matches
The Hidden Job of a Tennis Ball's Fuzz
A.explain_ko: 테니스공의 보풀이 공을 느리게 하고 회전을 걸게 해 준다는 글. 라켓·소재·프로 경기는 글에 나온 낱말로 만든 다른 초점.

A.question: Tally에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
A.passage: Every night after the Westbrook Public Library closes, a small robot named Tally goes to work. Tally was built by a team of engineers who wanted to help the librarians. The robot rolls slowly between the shelves. It reads the label on each book with its camera. If a book is in the wrong place, Tally marks it on a digital map. In the morning, the librarians check the map. Then they put the books back in the right places. Before Tally arrived, this job took three people a whole week. Now it is done in a single night. However, Tally cannot reach the top shelves, so people still check them by hand.
choices: 잘못 꽂힌 책을 직접 제자리에 옮겨 놓는다.
도서관이 문을 닫은 뒤 밤에 일한다.
A.explain_ko: Tally는 잘못 꽂힌 책을 지도에 표시만 하고, 아침에 사서들이 책을 제자리에 꽂는다. 나머지는 글과 일치한다.

A.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 __없는__ 문장은?
A.passage: Most wooden pencils have six flat sides. They are not round, and there is a good reason for this. ① A round pencil easily rolls off a desk, but a six-sided one stays in place. ② Some artists prefer soft pencils because they make dark lines. ③ The flat sides also give your fingers a comfortable place to rest. ④ In addition, more six-sided pencils can be cut from the same block of wood. ⑤ So less wood is wasted, and the pencils are cheaper to make. In short, a simple shape solves several problems at once. Next time you pick up a pencil, look at its sides!
A.explain_ko: 연필이 육각형인 까닭(구르지 않음·쥐기 편함·나무 절약)을 설명하는 글인데 ②는 부드러운 연심을 좋아하는 화가 이야기로 초점이 다르다.

A.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
이것은 할머니께서 나에게 주신 시계이다.
choices: This is the watch which my grandmother gave it to me.
This is the watch who my grandmother gave me.
This is the watch which my grandmother gave me.
This is the watch my grandmother gave me it.
This is the watch which gave my grandmother to me.
A.explain_ko: 사물 선행사 the watch를 받는 목적격 관계대명사 which. 관계절 안에 목적어 it을 다시 쓰면 틀리고, who는 사람에게 쓴다. 마지막 문장은 '시계가 할머니를 주었다'는 뜻이 된다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Hi. Do you have any cooking classes on Mexican food?
M: Yes. There's a tacos class on Friday and a soup class on Saturday.
W: Great. How much does each class cost per person?
M: They're both thirty dollars per person, including all the ingredients.
W: My son and I would like to take the tacos class together.
M: Sorry, the Friday class is full. But Saturday still has two spots.
W: Then we'll take the Saturday class. Is there a discount for children?
M: Yes. Kids under twelve get ten dollars off. How old is he?
W: He's eleven. Oh, and I'd like one of these aprons, too.
M: Sure. They're eight dollars each.
A.explain_ko: 수업료 30달러 + 아이 30달러에서 10달러 할인(20달러) + 앞치마 1개 8달러 = 58달러. 할인을 빼면 68달러, 앞치마를 빼면 50달러.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __pressure__
A.explain_ko: pressure는 '압력'. 즐거움(pleasure)·보물(treasure)·치수(measure)는 -sure로 끝나는 닮은 명사의 뜻.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __attitude__
A.explain_ko: attitude는 '태도'. 감사(gratitude)·고도(altitude)·위도(latitude)는 -titude로 끝나는 닮은 명사의 뜻.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __환경__
A.explain_ko: 환경은 environment. equipment(장비)·entertainment(오락)·experiment(실험)는 e-로 시작해 -ment로 끝나는 닮은 명사.

A.question: 다음 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
A.passage:
Excuse me, could you tell me where (A) _____?
If I (B) _____ a car, I would drive you to the airport.
choices: the bus stop is – will have
A.explain_ko: (A) 간접의문문은 의문사 + 주어 + 동사 어순이므로 the bus stop is. (B) 주절이 would drive인 가정법 과거이므로 if절은 과거형 had.

A.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: Look at the boy sitting quietly under the old tree.
My mom made me to clean my room before dinner last night.
I heard someone call my name in the dark hallway.
This is the writer whose novels are popular in many countries.
The broken window in the kitchen was fixed by my uncle.
A.explain_ko: 사역동사 make는 목적격 보어로 동사원형을 쓰므로 made me clean이 맞다. 나머지는 현재분사 수식·지각동사·소유격 관계대명사·과거분사 수식이 바르다.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage:
Imagine two students preparing for the same vocabulary test. The first student studies for three hours on the night before the test. The second student studies for only thirty minutes a day over six days. Both spend exactly the same amount of time. However, the second student usually remembers far more words a month later. Each time we return to information after a short break, our brain has to work a little to bring it back. This small effort makes the memory stronger and helps it last longer. Cramming may help you pass a test the next morning, but most of what you learn disappears quickly. So if you want to remember something for a long time, it is wiser to _____.
* cram: 벼락치기하다
choices: study for many hours in a single night
review everything on the morning of the test
take a long break after each lesson
spread your study time over several days
choose words that are easy to remember
A.explain_ko: 짧게 여러 날에 나누어 공부할 때 기억이 오래 간다는 글이므로 '여러 날에 걸쳐 나누어' 공부해야 한다. 하룻밤 몰아 공부·시험 당일 복습은 반대 내용, break는 지문 낱말을 쓴 오답.

A.question: tide pools에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
A.passage:
When the tide goes out, small pools of seawater are left behind among the rocks along the shore. These tide pools may look quiet. However, they are home to many creatures, including crabs, sea stars, and tiny fish. But life there is far from easy. For several hours each day, the animals living in the pools are cut off from the open sea. On sunny days, the water becomes warmer and saltier as some of it dries up in the heat. Sea birds hunting along the rocks can also spot an easy meal. To survive, many animals hide under stones or in narrow cracks until the water returns. When the tide comes back in, fresh seawater fills the pools again. It also brings new food with it.
* tide: 조수, 밀물과 썰물
choices: 썰물 때 바위 사이에 바닷물 웅덩이가 남는다.
맑은 날에는 물이 증발하면서 더 차갑고 덜 짜진다.
게, 불가사리, 작은 물고기 등이 산다.
밀물이 들어오면 새 먹이도 함께 들어온다.
A.explain_ko: 맑은 날에는 물이 일부 마르면서 더 따뜻하고 더 짜진다고 했으므로 '더 차갑고 덜 짜진다'는 틀리다.

A.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
A.given: In a roundabout, however, this kind of crash almost never happens.
A.passage:
In many cities, roundabouts are taking the place of busy crossroads. A roundabout is a circular intersection, and all cars move around its central island in the same direction. ( ① ) At a regular crossroads, a driver who runs a red light can hit the side of another car at full speed. ( ② ) Such side crashes are among the most dangerous kinds of traffic accidents. ( ③ ) Drivers must slow down to enter the circle, and cars never cross each other's paths directly. So any crash that does happen is usually a minor one. ( ④ ) Roundabouts also keep traffic moving. Drivers don't have to wait at a red light when no other cars are coming. ( ⑤ ) For these reasons, many city planners believe roundabouts are worth the extra space they need.
* roundabout: 원형 교차로
A.explain_ko: 옆을 들이받는 사고가 가장 위험하다는 문장 뒤, 원형 교차로에서는 그런 사고가 거의 없다는 주어진 문장이 오고, 그 까닭(속도를 줄이고 정면으로 길이 엇갈리지 않음)이 이어져야 한다.

A.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
내가 지금 정말 원하는 것은 긴 휴가이다.
choices: That I really want now is a long vacation.
Which I really want now is a long vacation.
What do I really want now is a long vacation.
The thing what I really want now is a long vacation.
What I really want now is a long vacation.
A.explain_ko: '~하는 것'은 선행사를 품은 관계대명사 what. That·Which는 선행사 없이 이 자리에 쓸 수 없고, What do I는 의문문 어순, the thing what은 선행사를 겹쳐 쓴 오류.

A.question: 다음을 듣고, Robot Rescue Challenge에 관해 언급되지 __않은__ 것을 고르시오.
A.script: W: Hello, students. This is Ms. Carter, the advisor of the Robotics Club. I'm excited to announce our school's first Robot Rescue Challenge. Teams will build robots that can find a toy figure inside a collapsed model building. The robot must then carry the figure safely out. Each team can have up to four members. No experience is needed, because we'll hold two free coding workshops next week. The challenge will take place in the gym on Saturday, November 14th. To join, fill out the form on the school website by this Wednesday. All robots must be built from the kits we provide. So you don't need to buy any parts. We hope to see many creative teams there.
A.explain_ko: 팀은 최대 4명, 장소는 체육관, 신청은 이번 수요일까지, 부품은 학교가 주는 키트로 만든다고 했지만 상품은 말하지 않았다.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __contribute__
A.explain_ko: contribute는 '기여하다'. 분배하다(distribute)·구성하다(constitute)·대체하다(substitute)는 어미가 닮은 동사의 뜻.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __adapt__
A.explain_ko: adapt는 '적응하다'. 채택하다는 철자가 한 글자 다른 adopt의 뜻, 지지하다·주장하다는 같은 동사 자리의 오답.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __효율적인__
A.explain_ko: 효율적인은 efficient. sufficient(충분한)·deficient(부족한)·magnificent(웅장한)는 -ficient/-ficent로 끝나는 닮은 형용사.

A.question: 어법상 __알맞은__ 문장의 개수는?
A.passage:
a. Walking along the beach, I found a strange shell half buried in the sand.
b. Not knowing what to say, she just smiled at the stranger.
c. I have two cousins, that live in a small town in Canada.
d. Feeling tiredly after the long trip, he went to bed early.
e. We visited the old castle, which built about six hundred years ago.
A.explain_ko: a·b가 맞다. c는 계속적 용법에 that을 쓸 수 없어 who, d는 분사구문 Feeling 뒤에 형용사 tired, e는 성이 '지어진' 것이므로 which was built가 되어야 한다.

A.question: 다음 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
A.passage:
(A) _____ the heavy rain, the outdoor concert went on as planned.
This is the small café (B) _____ my parents first met thirty years ago.
A.explain_ko: (A) 뒤에 명사구 the heavy rain만 오므로 전치사 Despite. (B) 뒤가 빠진 것 없는 완전한 절이고 장소 선행사이므로 관계부사 where.

A.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage:
Many dishes that are now proudly served in restaurants were born not from luxury but from the need to waste nothing. Fried rice, for example, began as a way to use rice left over from the day before. That rice had often become too dry to enjoy on its own. Bread pudding turned stale loaves into a sweet dessert. Likewise, countless soups were created by simmering bones and vegetable scraps that would otherwise have been thrown away. Cooks working with limited ingredients had to experiment, combining flavors in ways that wealthier kitchens never needed to try. Over generations, these thrifty solutions were refined until they became beloved parts of national cuisines. In this sense, scarcity has often acted less as a limit on cooking than as a source of creativity.
* stale: (빵이) 딱딱하게 굳은
* simmer: 뭉근히 끓이다
choices: how the need to save food gave birth to creative dishes
the health benefits of eating leftover food
why restaurant meals cost more than home cooking
the history of rice in traditional cooking
ways to reduce food waste in modern kitchens
A.explain_ko: 남은 재료를 버리지 않으려던 필요가 볶음밥·빵 푸딩·수프 같은 요리를 낳았다는, 부족함이 창의성의 원천이었다는 글. 음식물 쓰레기 줄이기·쌀의 역사는 지문 낱말을 쓴 다른 초점.

A.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 __없는__ 문장은?
A.passage:
In the weeks before a major race, many endurance athletes do something that seems strange. They train less. This practice, known as tapering, involves gradually reducing the amount of training while keeping a few short, intense sessions. ① On race day, athletes are usually advised to eat a light, familiar breakfast hours before the start. ② Months of hard training leave the body with tiny muscle injuries and tired energy systems, which cannot fully recover while the workload stays high. ③ By cutting back, athletes give their bodies time to repair this damage and to store extra fuel in their muscles. ④ As a result, they often arrive at the starting line feeling fresher and perform noticeably better. ⑤ Of course, tapering for too long can cause some loss of fitness, so coaches carefully plan its length.
* endurance: 지구력
A.explain_ko: 큰 경기 전에 훈련량을 줄여 몸을 회복시키는 테이퍼링을 설명하는 글인데 ①은 같은 경기 준비라도 경기 당일 아침 식사 이야기로 초점이 다르다.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage: When people imagine robots, they often picture machines with two arms, two legs, and a face, moving around like mechanical humans. Yet most robots doing real work today look nothing like us. In large warehouses, for instance, flat wheeled robots slide under entire shelves and carry them to workers. They never walk through the aisles to pick items one by one. Robot vacuum cleaners are shaped like low discs so that they can reach under sofas, where a human-shaped machine could never fit. On some farms, robots that pick strawberries roll along rails between the plants and use soft grippers instead of hands. Engineers have learned that copying the human body is often expensive and inefficient. After all, our bodies developed for survival, not for moving shelves or cleaning floors. The most successful robots, therefore, are designed around _____.
choices: the shape of the human body
the size of a typical home
the job they need to do
A.explain_ko: 사람 몸을 본뜨기보다 창고 선반 옮기기·소파 밑 청소처럼 할 일에 맞춘 모양이 성공한다는 글이므로 '해야 할 일'이 들어간다. 사람 몸 모양은 반대 내용.

A.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
그때 우리가 지도를 가져왔더라면, 길을 잃지 않았을 텐데.
choices: If we brought a map then, we would not get lost.
If we have brought a map then, we would not have gotten lost.
If we had brought a map then, we would not have gotten lost.
If we had brought a map then, we will not have gotten lost.
If we had bring a map then, we would not have gotten lost.
A.explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대는 If + had p.p., 주어 + would have p.p. 둘째 문장은 가정법 과거라 현재 사실의 반대가 되고, 나머지는 have·will·bring 형태가 틀렸다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Jessica, I've gone to the gym every day for a month, but my arms aren't any bigger.
W: Every single day? Are you working on the same muscles each time, Kevin?
M: Yeah, I do the same arm exercises daily. I thought more training would bring faster results.
W: Actually, that might be the problem. Muscles don't grow during lifting. They grow while you rest afterward.
M: Really? I always thought the workout itself made them stronger.
W: No. The workout causes tiny damage, and your body rebuilds the muscle thicker during recovery.
M: So training every day doesn't give it time to recover?
W: Exactly. Without a break, your body can't finish that process.
M: So how much rest does a muscle need?
W: Usually about two days. You could train your legs while your arms recover.
M: That makes sense. I'll make a new schedule this week.
choices: 근력 운동은 매일 같은 부위를 반복할수록 효과가 크다.
운동 전후에는 반드시 스트레칭을 해야 한다.
근육이 자라려면 같은 부위 운동 사이에 충분히 쉬어야 한다.
팔 운동보다 다리 운동을 먼저 해야 한다.
운동 일정은 전문 트레이너와 함께 짜야 한다.
A.explain_ko: 여자는 근육은 쉬는 동안 자라므로 같은 부위는 이틀쯤 쉬어야 한다고 말한다. 매일 반복은 남자의 처음 생각, 다리 운동은 쉬는 동안의 예로 나온 말.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __inherent__
A.explain_ko: inherent는 '본래 내재하는, 고유한'. 일관성 있는(coherent)·상속받을 수 있는(inheritable)·무관심한(indifferent)은 철자가 닮은 낱말의 뜻.

A.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __scrutinize__
A.explain_ko: scrutinize는 '면밀히 조사하다'. 요약하다(summarize)·공감하다(sympathize)·강조하다(emphasize)는 -ize로 끝나는 닮은 동사의 뜻.

A.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __취약한__
A.explain_ko: 취약한은 vulnerable. variable(변하기 쉬운)·venerable(존경할 만한)·available(이용할 수 있는)은 -able로 끝나는 닮은 형용사.

A.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: The number of students who walk to school has dropped sharply over the past decade.
Rarely does the committee change its decision once a final vote has been taken.
She spent the weekend reading novels, baking bread, and walking her neighbor's dog.
The fact that he had never left his hometown surprised everyone at the reunion.
The books that my grandfather left on the top shelf of his study is worth a fortune.
A.explain_ko: 주어의 핵심은 복수 The books이고 관계절은 수식어일 뿐이므로 is가 아니라 are. 나머지는 the number of + 단수 동사·부정어 도치·병렬·동격 that이 바르다.

A.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
A.passage: Tom insists that Jenny was at yesterday's meeting, but she _____ it: this morning she asked me what had been decided about the budget, even though the budget was the only topic discussed.
A.explain_ko: 오늘 아침 회의의 유일한 안건을 물었다는 근거로 '참석했을 리가 없다'는 과거 추측 can't have p.p. must have p.p.는 Tom의 주장 쪽(근거와 반대), should have p.p.는 추측이 아닌 '했어야 했는데'라는 비난, needn't have p.p.는 참석은 했다는 뜻, can't attend는 시제가 맞지 않는다.

A.question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
A.passage:
Researchers at Larkfield University recently asked a group of high school students to study a short science passage about how volcanoes form. Half of the students silently reread the passage for ten minutes. The other half spent the same time explaining its content aloud to an empty chair, as if they were teaching an imaginary classmate. When tested a week later, the explainers recalled nearly forty percent more information. More strikingly, they were far better at answering questions that required applying the ideas to unfamiliar situations. According to the researchers, explaining forces learners to organize scattered facts into a coherent account and exposes gaps in understanding that silent rereading allows them to overlook. Not only does the method cost nothing, but it also requires no partner, which makes it a practical tool for anyone studying alone.
* coherent: 일관성 있는
choices: Why Rereading Is the Key to Long-Term Memory
How Volcanoes Form and Why They Erupt
Group Study: Learning Better with Classmates
The Hidden Costs of Expensive Study Tools
Talking to an Empty Chair: A Simple Path to Deeper Learning
A.explain_ko: 빈 의자에게 소리 내어 설명한 학생들이 더 많이, 더 깊이 기억했다는 지어낸 연구의 글. 다시 읽기는 덜 효과적이었고, 화산은 공부 재료일 뿐, 짝이 필요 없다고 했으므로 그룹 공부도 오답.

A.question: the bone needle study에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
A.passage:
For decades, archaeologists assumed that the bone needles found at prehistoric sites were used mainly to sew warm clothing. A team at the Cardwell Museum of Natural History, however, has proposed a broader picture. After examining the wear patterns on sixty-three needles under a microscope, the team found that only about half showed the smooth polish typical of repeatedly passing through animal hide. The rest bore fine scratches more consistent with plant fibers, suggesting that they were used to make nets, baskets, or decorated items. Notably, several of the smallest needles had eyes so narrow that only a very thin thread could have passed through them. The researchers interpret this as evidence of detailed decorative work rather than survival needs alone. The team cautions, though, that their sample came from a single region and may not reflect practices elsewhere.
* hide: (동물의) 가죽
choices: 대부분의 바늘에서 동물 가죽을 통과하며 생긴 매끈한 광택이 나타났다.
고고학자들은 오랫동안 뼈바늘이 주로 옷을 꿰매는 데 쓰였다고 여겼다.
연구팀은 현미경으로 바늘 63개의 마모 흔적을 살폈다.
가장 작은 바늘 몇 개는 바늘귀가 매우 좁았다.
연구팀은 표본이 한 지역에서만 나왔다는 한계를 밝혔다.
A.explain_ko: 가죽을 통과하며 생긴 광택은 '약 절반'에서만 보였고 나머지는 식물 섬유 자국이었으므로 '대부분'은 틀리다.

A.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
A.given: As a result, your skin loses heat so fast that the water feels much colder than the air, though a thermometer would show the same number for both.
A.passage:
Step into a room at 20°C and you will probably feel comfortable. Step into a lake at exactly the same temperature, however, and you will soon begin to shiver. ( ① ) The difference lies not in the temperature itself but in how quickly heat leaves your body. ( ② ) Air is a poor conductor of heat. Thus the thin layer of air resting against your skin is warmed by your body and stays there, acting as a kind of invisible blanket. ( ③ ) Water, by contrast, conducts heat roughly twenty-five times faster than air, and its constant movement carries the warmed layer away before it can protect you. ( ④ ) What we experience as cold, then, is less a reading of the surroundings than a report on how rapidly we are losing heat. ( ⑤ ) Only by understanding this can we explain why swimmers, even in mild water, need far more energy to stay warm than people sitting in air of the same temperature.
* conductor: (열의) 전도체
A.explain_ko: 물이 따뜻해진 층을 쓸어 가 버린다는 문장 뒤에, 그 결과 피부가 열을 빨리 잃어 물이 더 차갑게 느껴진다는 주어진 문장이 오고, 차가움은 열을 잃는 속도의 신호라는 정리가 이어져야 한다.

A.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
그 도시를 세계에 알린 것은 바로 10년 전 시장이 복원한 오래된 다리들이었다.
choices: It was the old bridges restoring by the mayor ten years ago that made the city known to the world.
It was the old bridges restored by the mayor ten years ago that makes the city known to the world.
It was the old bridges restored by the mayor ten years ago that made the city known to the world.
It was the old bridges that restored by the mayor ten years ago made the city known to the world.
It was the old bridges restored by the mayor ten years ago that the city was made known to the world.
A.explain_ko: It was + 강조할 말(the old bridges restored by ~: 복원'된' 다리라 과거분사) + that + 나머지(made the city known). restoring은 능동, makes는 '알렸다'와 시제가 어긋나고, that을 분사 앞에 두면 어순이 깨지며, 마지막 문장은 that 뒤 절이 다리와 이어지지 않는다.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 대화하는 장소로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __whisper__
B.explain_ko: whisper는 '속삭이다'. 소리치다=shout, 대답하다=answer, 노래하다=sing.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __polite__
B.explain_ko: polite는 '예의 바른'. 인기 있는=popular(철자가 닮음), 정직한=honest, 게으른=lazy.

B.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __껍질을 벗기다__
B.explain_ko: peel은 '껍질을 벗기다'. pour=붓다, pull=당기다, fill=채우다(모두 짧은 요리·동작 동사).

B.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
B.passage: My little brother enjoys _____ paper planes in the park.
B.explain_ko: enjoy는 동명사를 목적어로 쓰므로 flying. to fly는 to부정사, fly·flew·flies는 동사 형태라 enjoys 뒤에 올 수 없다.

B.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: I have a few friends in my new class.
We had little rain last summer.
She drinks a lot of water every day.
There are a little cookies left in the jar.
Few people came to the meeting because of the snow.
B.explain_ko: cookies는 셀 수 있는 명사라 a little이 아니라 a few를 써야 한다. 나머지는 셀 수 있는 명사에 a few·few, 셀 수 없는 명사에 little, 둘 다에 a lot of를 바르게 썼다.

B.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage: Do you often feel sleepy after lunch? Many people do, and a short nap can help. A nap of about twenty minutes gives your brain a quick rest. After it, you can think more clearly and remember new words better. You may also feel less tired and more cheerful. But be careful about the length. If you sleep for more than thirty minutes, you can fall into deep sleep. Then it is hard to wake up, and you may feel even more tired. Also, try not to nap late in the afternoon. It can keep you awake at night. So keep your nap short and early.
choices: why people feel sleepy after lunch
the dangers of deep sleep at night
ways to remember new words better
the best time to go to bed at night
the good points of a short nap and how to take one
B.explain_ko: 짧은 낮잠의 좋은 점(머리가 맑아짐)과 길이·시간을 지키는 법을 함께 말한다. 점심 뒤 졸림·단어 기억은 일부 내용, 깊은 잠의 위험·잠자리 시간은 초점이 다르다.

B.question: Crayon Rescue Box에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
B.passage: Do you have old, broken crayons at home? Don't throw them in the trash. Bring them to the Crayon Rescue Box in the lobby of Oakdale Library. You can drop them off from March 2 to March 20. Volunteers will sort the crayons by color and melt them down. Then they will pour the wax into star and heart shapes. In April, the library will give the new crayons to children's hospitals in the area. Please remove the paper wrappers first if you can. Do not bring markers or colored pencils. Last year, people brought about 40 kilograms of crayons. Let's give old crayons a second life!
choices: 새 크레용은 4월에 지역 어린이 병원에 전달된다.
B.explain_ko: 'Do not bring markers or colored pencils.'에서 사인펜과 색연필은 가져오지 말라고 했다. 나머지는 지문 순서대로 일치한다.

B.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage: Have you ever heard your voice on a recording? Many people say, "That's not me!" There is a good reason for this. When you speak, the sound of your voice travels to your ears in two ways. One way is through the air outside your head. The other way is through the bones inside your head. The bones add deep, rich sounds to your voice. But a recording catches only the sound in the air. That is why your voice on a recording is _____ and thinner than your "inside" voice. Still, other people always hear your voice that way.
B.explain_ko: 뼈가 깊고 풍부한 소리를 더해 주는데 녹음에는 공기 소리만 담기므로, 녹음된 목소리는 더 높고 가늘게 들린다. deeper·richer는 지문 낱말을 쓴 반대 오답, louder·slower는 근거가 없다.

B.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
내일 비가 오면, 나는 집에 있을 것이다.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 동물 병원에 도착할 시각을 고르시오.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __disappear__

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __attach__
B.explain_ko: attach는 '붙이다'. 공격하다=attack, 성취하다=achieve, 참석하다=attend(철자가 닮은 낱말).

B.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __대신하다, 교체하다__
B.explain_ko: replace는 '대신하다, 교체하다'. repeat=반복하다, remove=없애다, reply=대답하다(모두 re-로 시작).

B.question: (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
B.passage:
My aunt has worked as a nurse (A) _____ ten years.
This hospital (B) _____ by her grandfather in 1975.
B.explain_ko: (A) 현재완료와 기간(ten years)에는 for. since는 시작 시점, during은 현재완료의 기간 표현으로 쓰지 않는다. (B) 병원이 '지어진' 것이고 1975년이므로 과거 수동태 was built.

B.question: 어법상 __알맞은__ 문장의 개수는?
B.passage:
a. The girl who lives next door plays the drums.
b. I need a chair to sit.
c. The movie which I saw it last night was boring.
d. She has something important to tell you.
e. This is the robot that cleans the floor by itself.
B.explain_ko: a(주격 who), d(형용사적 to부정사), e(주격 that)가 맞다. b는 '앉을 의자'이므로 to sit on, c는 목적격 관계대명사 뒤에 it을 다시 쓰면 안 된다. 3개.

B.question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage: A large white cloud may look as light as a feather, but it is actually very heavy. Scientists say that an average cloud holds about 500 tons of water. That is as heavy as about 100 elephants! So why doesn't it fall? The answer is that the water in a cloud is spread out into billions of tiny drops. Each drop is so small and light that it falls very slowly. At the same time, warm air that rises from the ground keeps pushing the drops up. When the drops join together and become too heavy, they can no longer stay up. Then they fall to the ground as rain.
choices: How Can Heavy Clouds Stay in the Sky?
Rain: The Best Gift from the Sky
Warm Air Makes the Weather Hot
B.explain_ko: 무거운 구름이 떨어지지 않는 까닭(작은 물방울, 올라오는 따뜻한 공기)을 설명한다. 코끼리·흰색·비·따뜻한 공기는 지문 낱말만 빌린 오답.

B.question: the Fern에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
B.passage: In the small town of Fernwick, people can pay with two kinds of money. One is the national dollar. The other is the "Fern," a paper note for use only in Fernwick. The Fern was created in 2019 by a group of local shop owners. They wanted people to spend their money in town instead of at big online stores. One Fern has the same value as one dollar. About 120 shops accept it. Each note shows a plant or animal that lives in the nearby forest. Visitors can change their dollars into Ferns at the town bank. However, Ferns cannot be changed back into dollars.
choices: 은행에서 다시 달러로 바꿀 수 있다.
지폐에는 근처 숲에 사는 동식물이 그려져 있다.
B.explain_ko: 마지막 문장에서 Fern은 다시 달러로 바꿀 수 없다고 했다. 달러를 Fern으로 바꾸는 것만 은행에서 된다.

B.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 __없는__ 문장은?
B.passage:
Almost everyone has had the hiccups at some time, and they can be really annoying. Why does this happen? Hiccups start in the diaphragm, a muscle under your lungs that helps you breathe. ① Usually, it moves smoothly, but sometimes it suddenly pulls down by itself. ② Then air rushes into your throat, and your vocal cords suddenly snap shut. ③ Many people enjoy singing because it helps them breathe deeply. ④ That quick closing makes the funny "hic" sound. ⑤ Eating too fast or drinking fizzy drinks can start this, but most hiccups stop on their own within a few minutes. If they don't, try holding your breath for a short time.
* diaphragm: 횡격막
* vocal cords: 성대
B.explain_ko: 딸꾹질이 생기는 과정(횡격막 → 공기 → 성대가 닫힘 → 소리)을 설명하는 글인데, ③은 노래와 깊은 호흡 이야기라 흐름과 무관하다. ④의 That quick closing은 ②를 받는다.

B.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
나는 그 소식을 듣게 되어 기뻤다.
choices: I was glad hear the news.
I was glad to hearing the news.
I glad to hear the news.
I was glad to hear the news.
I was glad to heard the news.
B.explain_ko: 감정 형용사 glad 뒤에 감정의 원인을 나타내는 to + 동사원형(to hear). to 빠짐, to hearing·to heard, be동사 빠짐은 오류.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 깃펜 체험 행사에 관해 언급되지 __않은__ 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Ethan, look at this flyer. The history museum is holding a quill pen workshop.
M: A quill pen? You mean writing with a feather like people did long ago?
W: Exactly. We'll make our own pens and write our names in old-style letters.
M: Sounds fun. When is it, and is it only for adults?
W: It's on Saturday, October 18, and it's open to anyone over twelve.
M: Great. Do we have to pay for it, though?
W: It costs five dollars, and that includes the ink and paper.
M: Not bad. Where in the museum is it held?
W: In the education room on the second floor. Let's go together.
B.explain_ko: 날짜(10월 18일 토요일), 참가 대상(12세 넘는 누구나), 참가비(5달러), 장소(2층 교육실)는 나왔지만 행사가 얼마나 걸리는지는 말하지 않았다.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __convenience__
B.explain_ko: convenience는 '편리함'. 관습=convention, 대화=conversation, 확신=conviction(모두 con-으로 시작하는 추상 명사).

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __ancestor__
B.explain_ko: ancestor는 '조상'. 후손=descendant(반대말), 이웃=neighbor, 동료=colleague(모두 사람을 가리키는 명사).

B.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __재료, 성분__
B.explain_ko: ingredient는 '재료, 성분'. instrument=도구·악기, incident=사건, influence=영향(모두 in-으로 시작하는 명사).

B.question: (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
B.passage:
(A) _____ made me laugh was the puppy's tiny hat.
Can you tell me (B) _____?
choices: What – when does the library open
That – when does the library open
B.explain_ko: (A) 선행사 없이 '~하는 것'이 주어가 되므로 관계대명사 What. That·Which는 선행사 없이 이 자리에 올 수 없다. (B) 간접의문문은 '의문사 + 주어 + 동사' 순서라 when the library opens.

B.question: 다음 중 어법상 __틀린__ 것은?
choices: The boy sitting next to me in class is from Canada.
The letter writing in French was hard for me to read.
I found a wallet lost by a tourist near the station.
Look at the yellow leaves falling from the old tree.
We visited a castle built about five hundred years ago.
B.explain_ko: 편지는 '쓰인' 것이므로 과거분사 written을 써야 한다. 나머지는 능동(sitting·falling)과 수동(lost·built)의 분사를 바르게 썼다.

B.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage: Trees growing at the edge of a forest live a very different life from those deep inside it. They face open fields, so they are hit by strong winds and bright sunlight every day. To survive, they grow thicker trunks and stronger roots. Many of them also grow branches low on the side facing the field. These thick walls of leaves slow down the wind before it enters the forest. They also keep the air inside cool and wet. In this way, the edge trees _____. When people cut down the edge trees to build roads, the trees left inside often begin to dry out. Some of them even fall over in the next storm. What looks like a simple line of trees is actually a shield for the whole forest.
choices: grow taller than the trees inside
turn the open fields into new forests
fall over more easily in storms
protect the trees deeper inside the forest
take water away from the trees inside
B.explain_ko: 가장자리 나무가 바람을 막고 안쪽 공기를 시원하고 촉촉하게 지켜 주며, 이 나무를 베면 안쪽 나무가 마르고 쓰러진다. 그러므로 '안쪽 나무를 보호한다'. 폭풍에 쓰러지는 것은 안쪽 나무이고, 나머지는 근거가 없다.

B.question: wax tablets에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
B.passage:
Long before paper became cheap, students in ancient Rome did their writing homework on wax tablets. A wax tablet was a flat piece of wood. A thin layer of dark wax was spread across it. Students wrote by scratching letters into the wax with a stylus. This was a pen-like tool made of metal or bone. One end of the stylus was sharp for writing, and the other end was flat. If students made a mistake, they used the flat end to smooth the wax and erase the letters. Two or more tablets were often tied together with string, so they looked like a small book. Tablets could be used again and again. However, they had one weakness: on a hot day, the soft wax could melt.
* stylus: 철필
choices: 틀린 글자는 철필의 뾰족한 끝으로 지웠다.
종이가 값싸지기 전에 학생들이 숙제에 썼다.
나무판 위에 얇은 밀랍 층을 입혀 만들었다.
더운 날에는 밀랍이 녹을 수 있었다.
B.explain_ko: 뾰족한 끝은 쓰는 데, 평평한 끝은 밀랍을 문질러 지우는 데 썼다. 두 끝의 쓰임을 바꾼 것이 오답.

B.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
B.given: On each of these trips, water freezes onto it and adds a new layer of ice.
B.passage: Hail is not just frozen rain that falls from storm clouds in summer. A hailstone begins its life as a tiny piece of ice high inside a thunderstorm. ( ① ) Strong winds rushing upward carry this piece of ice up and down through the cloud many times. ( ② ) Layer after layer, the hailstone grows bigger, much like an onion with many skins. ( ③ ) When it finally becomes too heavy for the winds to hold up, it falls to the ground. ( ④ ) If you carefully cut a large hailstone in half, you can see the rings of ice clearly. ( ⑤ ) By counting them, scientists can guess how many trips the stone made through the cloud. Some have more than twenty rings.
B.explain_ko: 주어진 문장의 these trips는 바람에 실려 '위아래로 여러 번' 오가는 움직임을 받고, 뒤 문장의 Layer after layer는 주어진 문장의 a new layer를 이어받는다. 그래서 ②.

B.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
내가 너라면, 그 일을 맡을 텐데.
choices: If I am you, I would take the job.
If I were you, I will take the job.
If I were you, I would took the job.
If I were you, I would take the job.
If I be you, I would take the job.
B.explain_ko: 현재 사실과 반대되는 가정은 If + 주어 + were, 주어 + would + 동사원형. am·be·will·would took은 형태 오류.

B.question: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
W: Good morning, students. This is Ms. Rivera, your school nurse, with a short message.
W: Lately, many of you have visited my office complaining of sore shoulders and backs.
W: In many cases, the cause is quite simple: your backpacks are far too heavy.
W: Experts say a backpack should weigh no more than ten percent of your body weight.
W: So next Monday and Tuesday, I'll be weighing backpacks at the main entrance before classes.
W: It only takes a few seconds, and I'll show you how to pack more wisely.
W: You can also leave unneeded books in your classroom lockers during the day.
W: Please stop by on your way in, and protect your back for years to come.
B.explain_ko: 어깨·허리 통증의 원인이 무거운 책가방이라며, 다음 주 월·화요일에 정문에서 책가방 무게를 재 준다고 알린다. 보건실·사물함은 말 속에 나온 낱말을 쓴 오답.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __acquire__
B.explain_ko: acquire는 '얻다, 습득하다'. 요구하다=require, 문의하다=inquire, 감탄하다=admire(끝 철자가 닮은 동사).

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __reluctant__
B.explain_ko: reluctant는 '꺼리는, 마지못한'. 관련 있는=relevant, 믿을 만한=reliable, 남아 있는=remaining(re-로 시작하는 형용사).

B.question: 다음 뜻을 가진 영어 단어는? __견디다, 참다__
B.explain_ko: endure는 '견디다, 참다'. ensure=보장하다, enable=가능하게 하다, enclose=둘러싸다·동봉하다(모두 en-으로 시작하는 동사).

B.question: 어법상 __알맞은__ 문장의 개수는?
B.passage:
a. I still remember the summer when we moved to the coast.
b. The town which I grew up has changed a lot since then.
c. She showed me the way how she solved the puzzle so quickly.
d. My uncle, who lives in Boston, sends me a postcard every year.
e. He lent me a mystery novel, that I finished in two days.
B.explain_ko: a(관계부사 when)와 d(계속적 용법 who)만 맞다. b는 장소 뒤 완전한 절이므로 where(in which), c는 the way와 how를 함께 쓰지 않고, e는 계속적 용법에 that을 쓸 수 없어 which. 2개.

B.question: (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
B.passage:
(A) _____ tired after the long hike, we went to bed early.
(B) _____ the heavy rain, the outdoor concert was not canceled.
B.explain_ko: (A) 주어 we가 '피곤함을 느낀' 능동이므로 분사구문 Feeling. Felt는 수동 뜻, Feel은 동사원형이라 안 된다. (B) the heavy rain은 명사구라 전치사 Despite. Although는 절 앞에 오는 접속사.

B.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage: Ask people why their work feels meaningful, and many will not mention their salary or even the tasks they perform. Instead, they talk about the people their work reaches. Consider a baker who rarely meets her customers. She may feel little pride in shaping dough before sunrise. Yet hearing that her bread was served at a neighbor's wedding, she often describes the same job in a completely new way. The work itself has not changed at all; what has changed is the worker's view of where it ends up. This suggests that meaning is not stored inside a job but grows from a visible link between effort and the lives it touches. Managers hoping to motivate a team, therefore, might do better to show workers the faces behind their results than to add more rewards.
choices: the importance of fair pay in keeping workers motivated
the daily routine of bakers who start work before sunrise
why workers should change jobs to find more meaning
ways for managers to reduce the number of daily tasks
meaning at work coming from seeing how one's work affects others
B.explain_ko: 일의 의미는 일 자체가 아니라 그 일이 다른 사람의 삶에 닿는 것을 볼 때 생긴다는 글이다. 보상(급여)은 오히려 덜 중요하다고 했고, 제빵사는 예시일 뿐, 이직·업무 줄이기는 근거가 없다.

B.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 __없는__ 문장은?
B.passage: Most of us assume that silence is the best condition for serious thinking. The truth, however, seems to be more complicated. ① Complete silence works well for tasks that demand close attention to detail, such as checking numbers. ② For tasks that call for fresh ideas, on the other hand, a moderate level of background sound can be helpful. ③ The gentle hum of a busy café, for example, distracts the mind just slightly, pushing it away from narrow focus and toward broader thinking. ④ Loud music played through earphones for long periods can permanently damage the tiny hair cells inside the ear. ⑤ Once the noise grows too loud, though, this benefit disappears. The brain then has to struggle simply to process what it hears.
B.explain_ko: 주변 소리의 크기와 생각하는 일의 관계를 다루는 글인데, ④는 이어폰 소음이 귀를 상하게 한다는 건강 이야기로 초점이 다르다. ⑤의 this benefit은 ②·③의 '도움'을 받는다.

B.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage: We usually treat pain as an enemy, something to be removed as quickly as possible. Yet pain plays a role that is easy to overlook. Imagine touching a hot pan without feeling anything: you would keep holding it until your skin was badly burned. People born without the ability to feel pain face exactly this danger, often hurting themselves seriously without noticing. Pain also continues after an injury for a good reason. A sore ankle makes you walk carefully, giving the damaged tissue time to heal. In this sense, pain is less a measure of damage than _____. Of course, pain that lasts long after healing is a different matter and needs treatment. But in most everyday cases, the ache we dislike is the body's way of looking after itself.
choices: a warning that protects the body from further harm
a sign that the body has stopped healing
a feeling that people should simply ignore
an exact record of how serious an injury is
a problem that always needs medical treatment
B.explain_ko: 뜨거운 팬을 놓게 하고, 다친 발목을 조심히 쓰게 해 회복할 시간을 주므로 통증은 '더 큰 해를 막는 경고'다. '손상의 정확한 기록'은 less a measure of damage와 반대, 나머지는 글과 어긋난다.

B.question:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
그가 지도를 확인했더라면, 길을 잃지 않았을 텐데.
choices: If he would have checked the map, he would not have gotten lost.
If he had checked the map, he had not gotten lost.
If he checked the map, he would not get lost.
If he had checked the map, he would not have gotten lost.
If he would have checked the map, he had not gotten lost.
B.explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대는 if절에 had p.p., 주절에 would have p.p. if절에 would have를 쓰거나 주절에 had p.p.를 쓰면 자리가 뒤바뀐 것이고, checked·would get은 현재 사실의 반대(가정법 과거)라 '확인했더라면 … 않았을 텐데'와 맞지 않는다.

B.question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Grace가 Tyler에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script:
M: Tyler is a high school student who can't fall asleep in complete silence.
M: Every night he plays music on his phone in bed until he feels sleepy.
M: But once the phone is in his hand, he starts checking messages and watching videos.
M: Lately he has been falling asleep well after midnight, almost every school night.
M: Yesterday his homeroom teacher even called home because he had dozed off in class.
M: His older sister, Grace, knows that music really does help him relax at night.
M: She also knows that sleeping with earphones in has been giving him sore ears.
M: She wants to suggest a way to keep the music but remove what keeps him awake.
M: In this situation, what would Grace most likely say to her younger brother, Tyler?
choices: How about leaving your phone outside your room and playing music on an old speaker?
You should stop listening to music at night if you really want to sleep well.
Why don't you keep your phone by your pillow but just turn the volume down?
I'll get you a new pair of earphones so you can listen in bed even longer.
Try going to bed even later so that you're tired enough to fall asleep quickly.
B.explain_ko: 음악은 지키되(조용하면 못 잠) 잠을 깨우는 휴대전화는 치워야 하고, 이어폰은 귀를 아프게 한다. 이 조건을 모두 지키는 것은 휴대전화를 방 밖에 두고 스피커로 음악을 듣는 방법뿐이다. 음악 끊기·휴대전화 곁에 두기·새 이어폰·더 늦게 자기는 각각 조건 하나를 어긴다.

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __compensate__
B.explain_ko: compensate는 '보상하다'. 경쟁하다=compete, 불평하다=complain, 완성하다=complete(모두 com-으로 시작하는 동사).

B.question: 다음 단어의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은? __tentative__
B.explain_ko: tentative는 '잠정적인'. 주의 깊은=attentive, 집중적인=intensive, 민감한=sensitive(모두 -tive 형용사).

B.question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
B.passage: Researchers at Calder University recently asked a simple question. Does a short night of sleep change how we read the people around us? They invited sixty adults to the lab on two separate occasions, once after a full night's rest and once after sleeping only four hours. On each visit, participants viewed photographs of strangers with neutral expressions and judged how friendly each person seemed. After the short night, participants rated the very same faces as noticeably less friendly and more threatening. They also reported less willingness to sit next to those strangers on a bus. Not only did their judgments shift, but most participants were also unaware of the change, insisting that the faces themselves looked different. The findings suggest that what a tired person interprets as unfriendliness in others may often be produced by his or her own exhausted brain.

B.question: the Halvern University study에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 __않는__ 것은?
B.passage: Recycling programs often fail not because people refuse to recycle but because they recycle the wrong things. A single greasy pizza box tossed into a paper bin can spoil an entire load, sending tons of usable material to a landfill. To see whether the shape of a bin could reduce such mistakes, researchers at Halvern University replaced the open-top bins in twelve office buildings. The new bins had openings shaped for the items they were meant to receive: a narrow slot for paper and a small round hole for cans. The results were striking. Over the next three months, wrongly sorted waste fell by nearly a third, while the total amount collected stayed about the same. Interestingly, signs explaining what belonged in each bin, tested earlier in the same buildings, had produced almost no change. So simple was the redesign that the university has since adopted it on its own campus.
choices: 연구진은 쓰레기통의 모양이 분류 실수를 줄일 수 있는지 알아보려 했다.

B.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
B.given: This gap between sight and sound is precisely what makes the method useful, since damage hidden beneath a green canopy can still be heard.
B.passage:
Counting the animals in a forest has traditionally required experts walking slowly along trails, a method that is slow and costly and whose results are easily affected by human presence. Researchers at the Westbrook Forest Institute have tested a quieter alternative. ( ① ) They hid forty small recorders across a mountain forest and let them run day and night for an entire year. ( ② ) Rather than identifying every species by ear, the team measured how varied and layered the soundscape was at each spot. ( ③ ) Places where birds, insects, and frogs filled different pitches and times of day turned out to be the places where field surveys had found the most species. ( ④ ) Sites recovering from logging, by contrast, produced thinner, more repetitive recordings, even when they looked green and healthy from above. ( ⑤ ) Such results suggest that a forest's health may be judged as much by listening as by looking.
